not_re_verified: Cold start is load-bound: six 42-round runs at 1-min load average 84-168 read 1.67-2.31x, and the article prints that range with the load. Every run is above the <= 1 target; none reproduces burgee's published 1.443x, which the spec records as a disagreement.

The spec's measurement commands run in a scratch directory holding the inline measure.mjs, so the stale-claim detector cannot execute them from the repo root (the corpus-wide class tracked by fix-unverifiable-spec-commands-2026-09-07).

growth_hook.why: The title follows the formula with a named target and two counts, then gives away its own weak point: like for like the family weighs 2.4x more. 'That is the flattering row' earns trust in the second paragraph, and the closing question sends the reader to count the accounts that can ship into their own tree. The cover reads '28 vs 9 / the 9 weigh 2.4x more', which is the like-for-like row and true; an earlier cover that paired 2.4x with 70 was false and was replaced in round 2.

security_correctness.why: Read as measurement correctness. Every tree, byte and maintainer figure re-ran from the article's own method lines, all 36 table cells are bytes / 1,024 rounded, and the derived figures (79 vs 70, 20 vs 9, six of nine, 2.38, 1,702 KB, +0.95% / +0.40%) check. Registry facts (sibling-only dependencies, node >=24, the 22.18 incumbent floor across the whole tree, publish times) and burgee's own figures at 7fb62c2 match. Five rounds of fixes got it here: four statements in the first draft were false, including the one the headline rested on.

structure_framing_voice.why: Landscape throughout and it concedes more than it has to: six layers where the incumbent installs fewer bytes, 2.4x on bytes like for like, Node 22.18 support, all three of burgee's unmet gates with re-runs, and an ETARGET window caused by the author's own release pipeline. The design surface is disclosed and linked, and 'no dependency outside the family, which is not zero' is exact. Small clarity costs remain: 'burgee' names both the engine package and the family, and the terminal-row aside is terse.

compatibility.why: Nothing is installed on the reader's behalf, so pass 3's matrix binds only loosely, and this goes past part 1's npm-only method: pnpm, yarn 1 and bun lockfiles resolve the same 70 / 28 / 9, with a spec row. Node minimums are stated for both sides. Held at the floor because the method block is npm-only and the article does not say that yarn 1 refuses the family below Node 24 where npm only warns.

reproducibility.why: The method block is safe to paste (a fresh mktemp directory, --ignore-scripts) and reproduces every figure; the spec carries measure.mjs, maintainers.mjs, bundle.mjs and cold.mjs inline, pins every family sibling, and records each disagreement with burgee's published figures instead of choosing one. Scored at the floor on the text before the versions went into the table; the family released twice during measurement, which is handled but is the reason drift is the article's live risk.
